title: France – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – Extension du terminal côté ville [EMT LANDSIDE] - Marché 1 : Plateformes multimodales
description: Le projet Évolution Modulaire du Terminal (EMT) vise à étendre et rénover les infrastructures terminales de l'Aéroport de Bâle-Mulhouse afin d'améliorer la qualité de service aux passagers. La présente consultation s'inscrit dans le 1er module du projet, intitulé « EMT Landside », qui comprend la construction d'une extension du terminal côté ville ; la rénovation dans le terminal existant ; la réalisation d'aménagements extérieurs. La réalisation de EMT Landside est organisée en trois (3) marchés de travaux distincts : Marché n°1 : Plateformes multimodales ; Marché n°2 : Extension du terminal et réaménagement des espaces existants ; Marché n°3 : Parvis piéton végétalisé. Le présent avis concerne le marché de travaux n°1 - Plateformes multimodales, portant notamment sur : - la création des rampes d'accès des parkings F1 et S1 ; - la réalisation des plateformes multimodales française et suisse ; - l'aménagement des locaux CFO/CFA dans les parkings F1 et S1 ; - l'aménagement de locaux destinés au Poste Central de Sécurité (PCS) et à la Police aux Frontières (PAF) ; - la démolition du viaduc ; - la déconstruction de la partie centrale du viaduc ainsi que des rampes d'accès Est ; - la viabilisation de la logistique provisoire ; - la réalisation des installations provisoires nécessaires au maintien des accès passagers. Phasage des travaux : Les prestations seront exécutées selon un phasage défini dans les documents de la consultation. Ce phasage tiendra notamment compte du maintien en exploitation des infrastructures aéroportuaires et de la continuité des accès. Les documents sont disponibles gratuitement, en version provisoire et à titre d'information (phase candidatures), à l'adresse : https://www.marches-securises.fr/. Informations complémentaires : Toutes les questions sont à poser via le profil d'acheteur https://www.marches-securises.fr/

title: CA18691 - RFQ 2026/48 - PEACEPLUS Roots Relationships Programme - Slieve Gullion DEA
description: To deliver a community-led Arts, Crafts and Heritage Capacity Building Programme in the Slieve Gullion DEA, working with community groups from the Forkhill and Newtownhamilton areas. The programme should use arts, crafts, cultural heritage and creative skills development as a vehicle for building organisational capacity, increasing skills and confidence, supporting knowledge exchange, and creating opportunities for participants to learn from one another through practical activities, shared experiences and networking opportunities. The programme should celebrate and explore the rich cultural and heritage assets of the area while creating opportunities for participants from different backgrounds to connect, collaborate and develop lasting relationships. Through shared learning and creative engagement, participants will strengthen both their individual skills and the sustainability of their community organisations. This project will serve as both a community development initiative and a peacebuilding mechanism, creating sustained and meaningful contact across communities while strengthening local organisations and promoting appreciation of the area's diverse cultural heritage. title: GB-Bootle: Stanley Road, Bootle - Roof Terrace Refurbishment Works
description: Plus Dane Housing wishes to undertake the refurbishment and renewal of the existing flat roof coverings to the roof terrace areas serving six residential properties at Stanley Road, Bootle. The Works generally include the removal of existing timber decking, support bearers, waterproofing membranes, insulation and vapour control layers; inspection and repair of the existing plywood roof deck where required; drainage improvements including new lead-lined drainage chutes and associated outlet works; threshold and upstand alterations; replacement parapet capping's; installation of a new Bauder reinforced bitumen membrane insulated warm roof covering system; provision of a new artificial grass roof terrace finish; reinstatement of roof-mounted items and handrail systems using proprietary support systems; and all associated ancillary, testing, certification and warranty works necessary to provide a complete watertight installation. Tenders must be submitted via the Delta e-tendering portal. Additional information: The contracting authority considers that this contract may be suitable for economic operators that are small or medium enterprises (SMEs). description: Business Oulu -liikelaitos (jäljempänä myös "BusinessOulu", "Tilaaja" ja "Hankintayksikkö") pyytää tarjouksia Oulun seudun työllisyysalueella järjestettävistä muutosturvakoulutuksista (jäljempänä myös "muutosturva55+ -koulutus") tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Pienhankintarekisteristä voidaan hankkia palveluita suoraan rekisteriin hyväksytyltä toimijalta tai kilpailuttamalla nopeutetulla aikataululla joko rajoitetulla menettelyllä tai kaikilta rekisteriin hyväksytyiltä tarjoajilta Hankinnasta kiinnostuneita ehdokkaita pyydetään jättämään osallistumishakemus Tarjouspalvelu.fi-portaalissa tämän osallistumispyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankinnasta julkaistaan tämä uusi ilmoitus teknisen virheen vuoksi. Edellinen ilmoitus avattiin hankintailmoitus 11.3.2025 ja siihen hyväksymispäätöksen (§49/2025, toimitettu 16.4.2025) saaneiden tarjoajien ei tarvitse jättää uutta osallistumisilmoitusta

Korm. rendelet 12–14. §) és az egyedi ajánlattételi felhívásban és szerződésben meghatározott követelmények szerint különösen: • A munkákkal és a szállítási útvonalakkal érintett épületrészek, közművek és környező területek állapotfelvételi dokumentációjának elkészítése. • Az Intézmény ellátásszervezési rendjéhez és a betegellátás folyamatosságához igazodó részletes térbeli és időbeli kivitelezési organizációs terv készítése (különösen a felvonulási és raktározási területek, a munkavégzési idők, a zaj- és porterhelés csökkentését szolgáló intézkedések, a személyek és gépjárművek be- és kiléptetése, az épületen belüli mozgás és anyagszállítás, valamint a beteg-, személyzeti és mentőforgalom, továbbá a menekülési útvonalak fenntartásának szabályozásával), egyeztetése és jóváhagyásra benyújtása. • Részletes ütemterv készítése, egyeztetése az Intézménnyel, a Műszaki üzemeltetővel és az Eszközbeszállítóval, valamint jóváhagyásra benyújtása a munkaterület átvételét megelőzően. Az egyeztetések lefolytatásáért, az érintett szereplők ellátásszervezési, üzemeltetési és eszköztelepítési követelményeinek ütemtervbe történő beépítéséért, valamint az ütemterv megvalósíthatóságáért és folyamatos aktualizálásáért, továbbá a kritikus úton lévő építési termékek határidőben történő beszerzéséért a Kivitelező felel. • A kivitelezés előkészítése és teljes időtartama során folyamatos egyeztetés az Intézménnyel és a Műszaki üzemeltetővel, a betegellátás folyamatosságának biztosítása, az ellátásszervezési követelmények és az intézményi működésből eredő kötöttségek figyelembevétele érdekében. Tervezett munkanemek felsorolása: A meglévő helyiségek és beszállítási útvonalak építészeti átalakítása; diagnosztikai berendezések fogadásához szükséges építési munkák és árnyékolások; komplex épületgépészeti rendszerek kivitelezése, így légtechnikai, hűtési-fűtési, szükség szerinti páratartalom-szabályozási, vízellátási és csatornázási munkák; komplex erősáramú energiaellátási rendszerek kivitelezése, beleértve a betáplálás, elosztás, kábelezés, védelem, földelés és EPH (egyenpotenciálra hozó, potenciálkiegyenlítő rendszer) kialakítását; a kapcsolódó gyengeáramú, tűzjelző és informatikai rendszerek szerelése, valamint a szükséges mérések, beszabályozások és próbaüzemek. A pontos tartalmat helyszínenként a terv határozza meg. A 321/2015 (X.30.) Korm. rendelet 46. § (3)-(5) bekezdésére figyelemmel ajánlatkérő felhívja a figyelmet, hogy, amennyiben a közbeszerzés tárgyának egyértelmű és közérthető meghatározása szükségessé tette meghatározott gyártmányú vagy eredetű dologra, illetve konkrét eljárásra, amely egy adott gazdasági szereplő termékeit vagy az általa nyújtott szolgáltatásokat jellemzi, vagy védjegyre, szabadalomra, tevékenységre, személyre, típusra vagy adott származásra vagy gyártási folyamatra való hivatkozást, a megnevezés csak a tárgy jellegének egyértelmű meghatározása érdekében történt, és megnevezés mellett a „vagy azzal egyenértékű” minden esetben értendő. Egyenértékű dolog megajánlása esetén az egyenértékűséget az ajánlattevőnek az ajánlatában igazolnia kell.

title: CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES, WHITEHORSE CADET TRAINING CENTRE WHITEHORSE
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Construction Management Services, Whitehorse cadet training centre whitehorse, yukon (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Whitehorse, Yukon. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES The objective of this contract is to recapitalize both vertical and horizontal infrastructure at the Whitehorse Cadet Training Centre (WCTC) through a multi-year program. The existing WCTC site includes a diverse portfolio of facilities comprising 39 buildings with a total floor area of approximately 5,000 m². These facilities include barracks with associated ablution areas, classrooms, a combined kitchen/dining/administration building, a large storage warehouse, and various workshops and auxiliary support structures. The recapitalization program will encompass the renovation of existing buildings, as well as the demolition and reconstruction of selected facilities, to modernize and enhance the overall functionality of the site. Project delivery will be undertaken using a Construction Management (CM) contract. The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project. To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the CM contract. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN: APN_NPYKCM01 Approximate Estimate: $50M Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent  will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS) 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors  that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors  that do not submit a proposal  will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Eric Ndayambaza Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada Eric.Ndayambaza@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Email: +(1) 343-576-9347 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Floor Refinishing Services
description: The U.S. Coast Guard Academy, New London, Connecticut, intends to procure hardwood basketball court floor refinishing services. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidental services necessary to perform annual screen-and-recoat maintenance for the approximately 17,422-square-foot Roland Hall Gymnasium court and, when included and funded, biennial services for the approximately 12,129-square-foot Billard Hall Gymnasium court. Services include cleaning, mechanically screening or abrading the existing finish as necessary, removing dust and debris, and applying an approved high-solids, low-VOC, oil-based commercial athletic-floor finish compatible with the existing coating system. Base CLIN services are limited to screen-and-recoat maintenance and do not include sanding to bare wood, repainting or restoration of court markings unless damaged by the Contractor or repairs other than repairs necessary to correct Contractor-caused damage. The requirement also includes an optional, firm-fixed-price per-square-foot CLIN for full refinishing of additional Government hardwood-floor areas, if authorized. The contractor shall protect existing court markings and Government property, comply with applicable safety and environmental requirements, coordinate the work schedule with the Contracting Officer�s Representative, and return each court to a clean, safe, uniform, and playable condition.

Installation of piping for wastewater, drainage, and sewerage at Geological Survey of Canada - Calgary (GSCC)
description: 3.1.1 The work covered by this service contract includes, but is not limited to, the provision of skilled labour, tools, and materials required to perform a wide range of tasks associated with wastewater, drainage, and sewerage piping systems throughout the facility. This includes installation, modification, replacement, testing, and commissioning of piping systems and associated components. 3.1.2 Services include site preparation; removal and disposal of existing piping, including the safe abatement and handling of asbestos-containing materials in accordance with all applicable regulations and approved procedures; installation of new piping systems; connection to existing infrastructure; and verification of proper system operation through inspection and testing. 3.1.3 The work also includes troubleshooting and repair of existing systems; ensuring proper flow, drainage, and system integrity; and confirming compliance with applicable codes, standards, and environmental regulations. All asbestos abatement activities must be carried out by qualified personnel following regulatory requirements and safety protocols. 3.1.4 The Contractor shall ensure that all work is performed with minimal disruption to facility operations and in coordination with NRCan’s facility management team. Documentation of completed work must be provided, including detailed descriptions of services performed, materials used, test results, identified deficiencies, and recommendations for corrective actions, system improvements, or preventative maintenance. 3.1.5 The installation of new roof drain piping, sewerage piping, and chemical-resistant laboratory piping includes labour, materials, fittings, valves, supports, hangers, anchors, penetrations, connections, testing, inspections, commissioning, restoration of affected surfaces, waste removal, and all other incidentals required to provide a complete and fully operational system.

title: SEPA PARKING LOT REPAVING AND REPAIRS
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) Project Title: SEPA Parking Lot Repaving and Repairs Solicitation Number: 89503511102026 The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Southeastern Power Administration (SEPA) is soliciting proposals from qualified contractors to perform parking lot repaving and repair services at its office facility. The required work shall be performed in accordance with the attached Performance-Based Statement of Work (PWS), which outlines the project scope, technical specifications, performance requirements, and expected outcomes. The applicable evaluation criteria are also included in the solicitation documents. Project Objective The objective of this acquisition is to restore the existing parking lot to a safe, structurally sound, properly drained, and fully functional condition suitable for use by government employees, visitors, and authorize vehicles. All work shall be completed in accordance with the requirements and specifications identified in the PWS. Location and Time of Performance Southeastern Power Administration, 1166 Athens Tech Drive, Elberton Ga. 30635. The available times are Monday-Friday 6:30am - 5:00pm Site Visit Prospective contractors are strongly encouraged, but not required, to participate in a site visit to assess existing conditions, evaluate the scope of work, and obtain a clear understanding of the project requirements before submitting a quotation. Failure to attend the site visit will not preclude a contractor from submitting a quotation or receiving consideration for award. The vendor has the option to conduct an on-site visit to determine the best approach for Southeastern Power project. Site visits will take place on November 19, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. Eastern Time and November 30, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Please email tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov with your preferred attendance time. Due to security requirements, all attendees must have a valid photo ID (i.e. State Driver's License) with REAL ID compliance to gain access to the site. All contractors must submit a list of attendees at least 24 hours in advance to: tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov. Please ensure that your list includes the name as it appears on your State ID and the company that will be attending. Contractors who do not possess a REAL-ID-compliant form of identification will be denied entry. Contract Type and Award SEPA anticipates awarding one (1) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract for the parking lot repaving and repairing project. The acquisition will be conducted using Simplified Acquisition Procedures in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13, as applicable. Award will be given to the responsible contractor whose proposal represents the best value to the government, based on the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation. Proposal Submission Deadline All proposals must be received by December 15, 2026, no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon), Eastern Standard Time (EST) Proposals may be submitted by mail to: 1166 Athens Tech Rd, Elberton, GA 30635 (addressed to: Tabitha Rambert) or electronically via email to: tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov Questions and Clarifications All questions, answers, requests for clarification, or inquiries concerning this solicitation will be provided to all offerors, posted on sam.gov by December 9, 2026, and shall be directed to both designated Contracting Officers: Primary: Tabitha Rambert, Contracting Officer (tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov) Alternate: Juvonna Mattox, Contracting Officer (juvonna.mattox@sepa.doe.gov) Any changes or clarifications affecting solicitation requirements will be communicated through an official solicitation amendment, as appropriate (via Sam.gov). Submission Timeline Site Visit: November 19, 2026, at 10:30am and November 30, 2026 @1:00 pm, Eastern Time Deadline for submission of all questions will be December 4, 2026 @12:00 pm Eastern time and Deadline for responses will be December 9, 2026, on Sam.gov Bid Submission Deadline: 3pm Eastern Time on December 15, 2026 Expected Decision Date: December 31, 2026 Vendor Start date: Within 30 days of Award Please submit all proposals to the CO via email at: tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov or via mail to:1166 Athens Tech Rd Elberton, GA 30635 before Bid Submission Deadline: 3pm Eastern Time on December 15, 2026. Vendor close-out date: NLT 2 Months from the vendor start date NOTE TO OFFERORS: The Statement of Work (SOW), applicable Wage Determinations, and Aeriel View are incorporated as attachments to this announcement. Offerors are responsible for thoroughly reviewing the solicitation and all accompanying attachments to ensure that their proposals comply with the stated requirements, and all are submitted by the specified deadline. Any amendments to the solicitation will be posted on this website. You are responsible for checking the website periodically. All offerors MUST be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of contract. The Government will evaluate proposals in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and applicable provisions of the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). The Government reserves the right to make an award to the responsible offeror, whose proposal represents the best overall value to the Government, considering the stated evaluation factors.

title: 6515--Patient Lifts and Slings for In Home Use
description: Patient Lifts & Slings for In Home Use This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 36C10G27R0002 is issued as a� request for proposal (RFP) for Patient Lifts and Slings (for in home use) as a uniform preferred product for Veterans, service members, and their families, who have earned through their military service to the United States. VHA accomplishes its mission by delivering patient-centered, personalized services that help Veterans readjust to civilian life and enhance their well-being. The Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) Veteran Health Administration (VHA), Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service (PSAS) has a need for Hydraulic Patient Lifts and Battery Powered Patient Lifts with Slings which are assistive devices that allows ability for caregivers to transfer Veterans between a bed, a chair or other similar resting places. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a supply source that will provide the contracted items to be utilized by Veterans Affairs Medical Centers (VAMCs). The objective is to ensure availability and consistency of products for nationwide usage and to obtain volume-based, standardized pricing. Standardization provides Veterans with high-quality continuity of healthcare and gives the VA concentrated buying power. This standardization initiative is in accordance with VHA Directive 1761.1. The Government seeks to establish an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract(s) with a period of performance of one (1) base year and four (4), one (1) year options. The requirement is solicited as a partial set aside for small business concerns for the Battery Powered Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition and Full and Open competition for the Hydraulic Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the procurement of these items is 339113 with a small business size standard of 800 employees. Please identify your business size in your response based upon this standard. The government will only establish award(s) with the Offeror(s) that meets all requirements of the solicitation. The award(s) resulting from this solicitation will be made based on the best overall proposal that is determined to be the most beneficial to the Government (i.e., best value). Place of Performance: Multiple locations throughout the continental US, Hawaii and all US Territories; delivery location(s) will be defined per each order. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at� www.acquisition.gov. All vendors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database https://sam.gov. This acquisition is being conducted in accordance with the procedures in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services in conjunction with FAR Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation, FAR Part 16.504 Indefinite-quantity Contracts, and FAR Part 16.505 Ordering. Proposals must be submitted in accordance with the instructions provided under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors Commercial Items. The proposal must be submitted no later than December 15, 2026, 12 PM EST unless this date is changed via a formal solicitation amendment. The contractor shall submit an electronic (email) copy of the proposal to both Noel Echevarria, Contract Specialist at Noel.Echevarria@va.gov and Brian Love, Contracting Officer at Brian.Love@va.gov. The Government is not responsible for confirming receipt. Any proposal received after the specified date and time will be unresponsive and shall receive no further consideration. In accordance with FAR 52.212-1(c), Offerors are responsible for submitting offers and any modifications or revisions to the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation. These e-mail addresses identified for the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer are the Government office designated in the solicitation as defined in FAR 52.212-1(c)(1) for timely receipt of proposals. Exceptions for late receipt of electronic submissions are specifically outlined in FAR 52.212-1(c)(2).

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) DDG 1000 Class Modernization: USS Michael Monsoor (DDG 1001) Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) Depot Modernization Period (DMP); Large Missile Vertical Launch System (LMVLS) Heavy Lift and Industrial Installation
description: 1.0 PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE PAE Maritime, on behalf of the dPAE Combatants/ DDG 1000 Class Program Office (PMS 500), is conducting market research to assess industry capabilities, engineering rigor, and shipyard infrastructure necessary to accomplish the industrial integration and installation of the Large Missile Vertical Launch System (LMVLS) aboard the USS Michael Monsoor (DDG 1001). The primary objective of this RFI is to evaluate prospective offerors' specific technical expertise, dry dock/pier-side heavy-lift capabilities, dimensional control methodologies, and integrated production scheduling to execute the installation of a pre-manufactured ~600-ton LMVLS module and associated Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) warfare alterations. The questions contained in Section 3.0 are specifically structured to allow industry respondents to demonstrate their understanding of the unique structural, spatial, lifting, and combat systems complexities associated with this depot modernization period. 2.0 TECHNICAL BASELINE & REQUIREMENT SUMMARY Key technical parameters within the DDG 1001 CPS DMP include: 2.1 Ship Particulars Vessel: USS Michael Monsoor (DDG 1001) Length Overall (LOA) / LBP: 186 m (610 ft) / 182.9 m (600 ft) Beam (Maximum): 24.6 m (80.7 ft) Draft (Navigational / DWL): 8.4 m (27.6 ft) / 7.0 m (23.0 ft) Hull Form & Superstructure: Wave-piercing tumblehome hull; steel hull structure with composite deckhouse; integrated power system (IPS). 2.2 LMVLS Pre-Manufactured Assembly Profile (GFM) The Government plans to deliver the LMVLS as Government-Furnished Material (GFM) as a fully out-fitted, pre-manufactured modular block. The industrial effort will require rigging, lifting, transferring, lowering, and setting the ~600-ton LMVLS module into the hull pocket within tight spatial and angular tolerances. Additional specifications include: Envelope Dimensions: Approximately 44� 7� Length � 20� 8� Width � 41� 1� Height. Total Lift Weight: Approximately 600 Long Tons (LT). Component Integration: Four (4) launch tubes housing Advanced Payload Modules (APMs) and All-Up Round Canisters (AUR-C), integral shock-isolation foundation assemblies, multi-level bulkheads (down through L5), decks, pre-installed outfitting, and weather deck / 01-level hatch structures. Installation Location: Forward Stack 1400 (reclaimed forward space following MT 61 AGS complete removal). 3.0 TECHNICAL CAPABILITY QUESTIONNAIRE Interested sources are requested to provide detailed technical narrative responses, supported by engineering calculations, facility specifications, past performance references, and risk mitigation methodologies, addressing each section below. Section A: Heavy Lift, Rigging & Facility Engineering Capabilities Lifting Infrastructure & Capacities: Detail your primary crane assets (gantry, floating, portal, or crawler) capable of hoisting and swinging a 600-ton (approx. 1,344,000 lbs) rigid modular assembly. Provide the specific crane load charts demonstrating rated capacity at the required operating radius and minimum hook height necessary to clear DDG 1001�s deck edge, bulwarks, and adjacent deckhouse structures (taking into account the 41� 1� module height plus lifting beam/spreader bar rigging height). If utilizing a floating crane for the LMVLS, confirm that the selected crane has the clearance to transit under any bridges necessary to arrive at your shipyard. Specify whether the 600-ton lift will be executed in dry dock or pier-side, and detail the structural load-bearing capacity (pounds per square foot / ground bearing pressure) of the quay wall, pier apron, or dry dock wing walls supporting the crane footprint during maximum outrigger or track loadings. Rigging, Stability & Tandem Operations: Describe your concept for the lift rigging assembly (spreader frames, equalizing grommets, dynamic load monitoring systems) to eliminate torsional deflection, racking, and localized stress concentrations on the pre-assembled LMVLS module during the pick. If a tandem or multi-crane lift is planned, provide your operational methodology for synchronous motion, hook travel rate synchronization, and emergency load re-distribution mitigation. Address environmental limits: What are your maximum allowable wind speed, wave/surge motion (if using floating derrick/crane barges), and tidal envelopes for executing this precision lift? Ship Mooring, Ballast & Hull Stability During Module Placement: DDG 1001 possesses a unique wave-piercing tumblehome form with strict naval architectural stability limitations. Describe your approach to calculate, model, and monitor ship list, trim, draft changes, and metacentric height during the removal of the forward AGS weight and subsequent setting of the 600-ton LMVLS module (whether afloat at a pier or during block contact in dry dock). Section B: Precision Alignment, Metrology & Structural Integration Dimensional Control & Metrology Framework: The LMVLS module must interface with existing ship structure, pre-established shock-attenuation foundations, and tight topside radar cross-section (RCS) deck tolerances. Describe your advanced metrology procedures (e.g., 3D laser scanning, photogrammetry, laser tracking) from initial ship condition surveying through pre-lift verification and final post-weld alignment. Section C: Industrial Coordination, Schedule Phasing & AIT Co-Existence Integration of Alteration Installation Teams (AIT) & System OEMs: Installation of the CPS LMVLS requires extensive concurrent work by Government labs and weapon system prime contractors (e.g., Raytheon, Lockheed Martin, NAVWAR). Detail your approach for managing space conflicts, shared lifting/crane services, security access controls for classified weapon compartments, and jurisdictional hand-offs between shipyard trades and specialized weapon installers. Subcontracting, Teaming & Industrial Workshare: If teaming or significant subcontracting (>20%) is required to satisfy heavy crane, precision metrology, or specialized welding capabilities, outline your proposed organizational hierarchy, prime contractor oversight model, and quality assurance audit procedures. If responding as a Small Business prime under FAR 52.219-14, explicitly demonstrate how your organization will perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing and direct industrial labor. Section D: Risk Assessment, Lessons Learned & Resource Management Critical Technical & Industrial Risks: Identify what your organization views as the top three (3) critical technical failure modes or schedule risks during the LMVLS module installation (e.g., crane unavailability, structural distortion exceeding cell launch tolerances, GFM delivery mismatches, dry dock schedule creep). For each identified risk, provide specific, mitigation strategies and fallback procedures. 4.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS & SUBMISSION GUIDELINES 4.1 Content & Page Limitations Cover Sheet: CAGE Code, SAM UEI, MSRA/ABR status, business size under NAICS 336611 (Ship Building and Repairing), primary technical and contracts POCs. Volume I (Technical Capability Narrative): Not to exceed five (5) pages, addressing all questions in Section 3.0. Volume II (Facilities, Equipment & Crane Load Charts): Not to exceed five (5) pages, containing facility schematics, dry dock certified dimensions, dock loading curves, and relevant crane radius/load capacity charts. 4.2 Marking of Proprietary Information Respondents must clearly mark and isolate any proprietary data, trade secrets, or commercial pricing/cost methodologies. The Government will handle properly marked data in accordance with applicable statutory regulations and protect it as Business Sensitive. 4.3 Inquiries & Submission Points of Contact Submissions shall be delivered electronically via DoD SAFE or secure email no later than the time and date specified in the official SAM.gov synopsis: Procuring Contracting Officer: Brian Romano, PAE M 025 (brian.c.romano.civ@us.navy.mil) Contract Specialist: James Thom

description: Patient Lifts & Slings for In Home Use This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 36C10G27R0002 is issued as a� request for proposal (RFP) for Patient Lifts and Slings (for in home use) as a uniform preferred product for Veterans, service members, and their families, who have earned through their military service to the United States. VHA accomplishes its mission by delivering patient-centered, personalized services that help Veterans readjust to civilian life and enhance their well-being. The Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) Veteran Health Administration (VHA), Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service (PSAS) has a need for Hydraulic Patient Lifts and Battery Powered Patient Lifts with Slings which are assistive devices that allows ability for caregivers to transfer Veterans between a bed, a chair or other similar resting places. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a supply source that will provide the contracted items to be utilized by Veterans Affairs Medical Centers (VAMCs). The Government seeks to establish an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract(s) with a period of performance of one (1) base year and four (4), one (1) year options. The requirement is solicited as a partial set aside for small business concerns for the Battery Powered Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition and Full and Open competition for the Hydraulic Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the procurement of these items is 339113 with a small business size standard of 800 employees. The award(s) resulting from this solicitation will be made based on the best overall proposal that is determined to be the most beneficial to the Government (i.e., best value). No changes have been made to the content of any of the attachments, rather simply updating file format to ensure usability. The purpose of Amendment 0001 is to: 1) update instruction in Section J, Attachment L1 Rev 01, Part A, Paragraph 4.1.1 to clarify marking requirements and Part B Paragraph 2.3.1 regarding adverse past performance; 2) revise applicable Attachments to reflect updates to CUI markings; 3) revise language in Section J, Attachment M1 Rev 01, Part A, Paragraph 1.4 and Part B, Paragraph 1.2 clarifying Evaluation Process; 4) update Attachment C2 Table 3 to remove the requirement to include DFAS DoDAAC and POC information; 5) provide a revised Attachment 01 to correct the RFO number as well as update the Function description of the Management Analysts (Acquisition), Senior, BLS SOC 13-1111(Key). The due date for proposals remains unchanged: see Block 9 of the SF33. Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF), Airborne Systems Integration (ASI) Division intends to issue a competitive, total small business set-aside Request for Offers (RFO) under the SeaPort Next Generation (NxG) Multiple Award Contract for Airborne Systems Integration (ASI) Technical/Project Management Support (TPMS). The resulting Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee task order will provide technical project-management, data-management, and acquisition support for ASI Division requirements. Support includes project planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout; division-level planning and performance reporting; data analytics, metrics, and repeatable best practices. The effort supports multiple defense acquisition programs and weapons systems, including�but not limited to�VH-92A, E-6B, unmanned carrier aviation, counter-uncrewed systems, V-22, and Naval Sea Systems Command Integrated Warfare Systems Program Executive Office requirements. Performance is anticipated at Government sites in St. Inigoes, Maryland, and Patuxent River, Maryland, with limited contractor-site performance within 50 drivable miles of NAWCAD WOLF. A Secret Facility Clearance Level is required.

title: National Veterans Sports Programs & Special Events National Veterans Golden Age Games (NVGAG) National Veterans Creative Arts Festival (NVCAF) Transportation
description: This Performance Work Statement (PWS) defines the requirements for transportation services under an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. The contract supports two national?level Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) programs: � The National Veterans Golden Age Games (NVGAG), including annual site visits and event transportation during the ordering period. � The National Veterans Creative Arts Festival (NVCAF) for designated event years. This IDIQ provides a unified scope of transportation services required to support recurring national VA events. Each task order will define the event year, schedule, required vehicle quantities, routing requirements, and operational details. Except where a minimum is stated, passenger counts and quantities in this PWS are planning figures; each task order will state the firm requirements. 1.1 National Veterans Golden Age Games (NVGAG) NVGAG is a national senior adaptive rehabilitation program promoting fitness, independence, and quality of life for older Veterans. It features multi?event athletic competitions and recreational activities for Veterans with varying levels of physical ability. NVGAG also serves as a qualifying event for participation in the National Senior Games. 1.2 National Veterans Creative Arts Festival (NVCAF) The National Veterans Creative Arts Festival empowers Veterans to improve their mental and physical health through therapeutic creative arts experiences. The event reinforces the VA�s commitment to whole health, recovery-oriented care, and Veteran-centered services by celebrating resilience, achievement, and personal growth. Showcasing the intersection of artistry and healing, the event features National Veteran medalists invited for their artistic achievements and therapeutic use of the arts.

The Nazario Courthouse will remain fully operational throughout the duration of the Seismic Retrofit. To ensure minimal disruption to Government operations, the work will predominantly be executed after business hours. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Government�s requirements for access and security. Additionally, the General Contractor will be required to complete this project in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications that will be issued for this project. Contract Type: The contract type for this procurement will be Firm-Fixed price. The line item schedule will include a lump sum item for the Base and Options. Price: The total magnitude of this project at award is between $40,000,000 and $50,000,000. Selection and Schedule: The General Contractor will be selected through a procurement method developed in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation (Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36 Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36). The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Evaluation process. During Phase I, prospective firms must submit technical qualifications detailing their experience with comparable efforts and previous records of past-performance. In Phase II, selected General Contractors shall demonstrate their operational strategy and planned subcontracting framework. Evaluation of Phase II technical submissions will be conducted in full before the Government reviews the price proposal. GSA anticipates award of a contract for these services in August 2027. The period of performance for the proposed contract will be for approximately forty six (46) months upon issuance of notice to proceed. NAICS: This procurement will be conducted under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220--Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business size standard is an average annual sales and receipts for the past three (3) years that are equal to or less than $45,000,000. description: SOLICITATION NOTICE MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF). Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order. LOCATIONS OF WORK The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in: � Bethesda, Maryland, � Frederick, Maryland, � Poolesville, Maryland, � Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, � The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana. NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. PSC Code: Y1JZ The corresponding small business size standard is $45 million. The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively. ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns. NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of: Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves. The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and Participants in the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. The solicitation will identify the anticipated distribution of the sixteen (16) reserve awards among the applicable small business and socioeconomic categories and will establish the eligibility requirements applicable to each reserve. NIH anticipates approximately four (4) awards in each socioeconomic reserve. Offerors must meet all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the category under which they submit an offer. BONDING CAPACITY Offerors competing for an unrestricted/full-and-open award shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $100 million for a single project; and $300 million aggregate bonding capacity. Offerors competing for an award under a small business reserve shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $3 million for a single project; and $10 million aggregate bonding capacity. The solicitation will establish the specific documentation required to demonstrate bonding capacity. Performance and payment bond requirements applicable to individual construction task orders will be established in accordance with the solicitation, resulting contracts, applicable law and regulation, and the requirements of each task order. SMALL BUSINESS ELIGIBILITY AND JOINT VENTURES Offerors seeking an award under a small business reserve must satisfy all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the applicable reserve category and NAICS code. The solicitation will identify any documentation required to establish an offeror's eligibility for the applicable small business or socioeconomic category. Small business concerns intending to submit an offer as a joint venture must comply with all applicable SBA joint venture requirements, including applicable requirements governing SBA-approved Mentor-Prot�g� relationships. Prospective offerors should consult current SBA regulations and guidance concerning joint ventures and the SBA Mentor-Prot�g� Program at www.sba.gov. The $3 billion ceiling applies collectively to all MACC contracts and is not a per-contractor ceiling. The anticipated ordering period will consist of one eight-year ordering period. There is no anticipated annual or individual-contractor ceiling other than limitations established by the terms of the resulting contracts and individual task orders. MACC holders will remain eligible to compete for task orders, subject to the terms and conditions of their contracts, until expiration of the ordering period or exhaustion of the aggregate MACC ceiling, whichever occurs first. TASK ORDERS All work under the MACC will be authorized through individual task orders. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis and will be separately priced. Each task order will establish the applicable scope of work, specifications and drawings, period of performance, applicable wage determination, bonding requirements, and other project-specific requirements. Task orders may be competed among all eligible MACC holders or restricted to eligible small business MACC holders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated maximum value of an individual task order is $800 million. Eligibility to compete for individual task orders may be subject to project-specific requirements, including required bonding capacity. The $1,000 guaranteed minimum is a contractual minimum obligation and should not be interpreted as establishing the minimum dollar value of all future task orders. title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: UPDATE #1 � Amendment #0001 to the RFP was released on October 22, 2026. UPDATE #2 � Amendment #0002 to the RFP was released on October 26, 2026. UPDATE #3 - Amendment #0003 to the RFP was released on November 20, 2026. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

This Sources Sought Notice is not to be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Mobile District to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. As part of market research, this Sources Sought notice is to determine whether an adequate number of qualified, interested vendors exist that can provide the required goods and services required. Additionally, USACE intends to surveil the market to determine the availability of qualified small business contractors to perform these services and to determine socioeconomic classifications (Small Business, HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, Women Owned Small Businesses, etc.) associated with each. The primary North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code applicable to this requirement is 332710, the small business standard for which is 500 employees. While 332710 is the primary NAICS, capabilities from firms operating under 333611 or 811310 are also highly encouraged to respond.[PT2] [JW3] Draft Scope: Market Research and Sources Sought Notice for information on capability and availability of potential contractors interested in proposing on a Firm Fixed Price Contract for inspecting and re-babbitting [PT4] [JW5] a quantity of 20 thrust shoes. The shoe segments are a truncated pie shape with dimensions approximately 19.26 inches long, 23.72 inches wide (at OD), and 13.43 inches wide (at ID). The bearing shoes are 8 inches thick, including a babbitt layer of 0.13 inches. The scope of work consists of: Provide round-trip transportation of the thrust shoes between the project and refurbishment facility. Perform as-received inspections and document the condition for every shoe. Conduct pre-babbitt NDT (visual (VT) and liquid penetrant (PT)) and obtain Government acceptance. Remove old babbitt and prepare the shoes. Restore the steel backing / backside of the shoes. Re-babbitt the running surface of the shoes by pouring new babbitt. The new babbitt metal shall be new material conforming to ASTM B 23 Alloy 2. The tin used for tinning shall be 99 percent pure. Use of reclaimed metal will not be acceptable. Restore functional features and final geometry of the shoes. Perform final babbitt-bond NDT (ultrasonic test (UT) and liquid penetrant (PT)) of the shoes. Final inspection, reporting, and Government release of the shoes. Preserve and return the completed shoes. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the government in making appropriate acquisition decisions. QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY & RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Industry feedback is requested as follow: On the first page, please indicate whether your firm is interested in providing a quote for this requirement? (Yes / No) On the first page, please provide your company�s name, address, Cage code, UEI, primary points of contact (to include telephone number(s) and e-mail address. On the first page, please state your business size/classification under NAICS 332710 and any SBA certifications (i.e. any designations such as Small Business, HUBZone, Section 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, and Women Owned Small Business) on first page of submission. Veteran-owned firms should state their SBA VetCert status as well. Please provide a Capabilities Statement on how the company can provide the services stated within the drafted Scope of work. Describe no more than (3) similar projects for like services as described above. Provide the project name, description, location, overall dollar value, date services completed or percentage of completion. The above requested information shall not exceed a total of eight (8) pages on 8.5" x 11" paper, 12-point Times New Roman font, with a minimum of one (1) inch margins all around. In the subject line of your email state: Response to Inspect and Re-Babbitt Thrust Shoes for Richard B. Russell Powerhouse, Elberton, GA, Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District Responses shall be submitted via email to CTHYDRO-Proposals@usace.army.mil and Phuc (Peter) Dang at Phuc.d.dang@usace.army.mil. Responses are due no later than 12/15/2026, 2:00 p.m. CDT. Responses received after this date and time may not be reviewed. DISCLAIMER There is no solicitation available currently; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. Responses to this Sources Sought are not quotes, proposals, or bids on which USACE can issue a contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses to this Sources Sought. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding, and USACE will not pay for information received. Neither unsolicited proposals nor other kinds of offers will be considered in response to this Sources Sought Notice. This Source Sought Notice does not create an obligation on behalf of the Government to make an award of any contract pursuant to this announcement, so do not submit pricing information. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation and its supplements. It is the contractor�s responsibility to monitor the Government Point of Entry for the release of any solicitation. [PT1]KO concurs that the PSC and NAICS. [PT2]This language is being introduced to ensure that we do not miss specialty Hydro-turbine repair firms that don�t self -identify primarily as standard �machine shops�. Please get concurrence from the PM prior to release. [JW3]I concur. [PT4]To minimize uncertainty, can we provide additional technical details & specifications as contractors cannot accurately determine if they have the capability to respond unless they know the physical scale and specifications of the work. Details to consider adding includes: Adding Physical Dimensions/Weight: Provide the approximate size (diameter/width), thickness, and estimated weight of each of the 20 thrust shoes. Specify Babbitt Material & Method: State the required Babbitt alloy (e.g., ASTM B-23 Grade 2 Tin-Based Babbitt) and whether centrifugal/spin casting is required or if static casting is acceptable. Clarify NDT (Non-Destructive Testing) Requirements: State whether ultrasonic testing (UT) for bond integrity (e.g., per ASTM E114 or ISO 4386) or liquid penetrant testing (PT) is required. title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: UPDATE #1 � Amendment #0001 to the RFP was released on October 22, 2026. UPDATE #2 � Amendment #0002 to the RFP was released on October 26, 2026. UPDATE #3 - Amendment #0003 to the RFP was released on November 20, 2026. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: General Contractor for the Seismic Retrofit Project at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse, San Juan, Puerto Rico
description: Description The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, Capital Projects Contracting Division, is pleased to announce the issuance of a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a highly qualified Contractor who can provide Construction Services to perform a Seismic Retrofit at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse (Nazario Courthouse) located at 150 Carlos Chardon Avenue in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Nazario Courthouse will remain fully operational throughout the duration of the Seismic Retrofit. To ensure minimal disruption to Government operations, the work will predominantly be executed after business hours. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Government�s requirements for access and security. Additionally, the General Contractor will be required to complete this project in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications that will be issued for this project. Contract Type: The contract type for this procurement will be Firm-Fixed price. The line item schedule will include a lump sum item for the Base and Options. Price: The total magnitude of this project at award is between $40,000,000 and $50,000,000. Selection and Schedule: The General Contractor will be selected through a procurement method developed in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation (Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36 Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36). The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Evaluation process. During Phase I, prospective firms must submit technical qualifications detailing their experience with comparable efforts and previous records of past-performance. In Phase II, selected General Contractors shall demonstrate their operational strategy and planned subcontracting framework. Evaluation of Phase II technical submissions will be conducted in full before the Government reviews the price proposal. GSA anticipates award of a contract for these services in August 2027. The period of performance for the proposed contract will be for approximately forty six (46) months upon issuance of notice to proceed. NAICS: This procurement will be conducted under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220--Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business size standard is an average annual sales and receipts for the past three (3) years that are equal to or less than $45,000,000. All offerors are required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) at the time of offer submission, and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract. Interested offerors - See all attached solicitation file packages for full details. Some of the solicitation documents are Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). To access these documents your company must request access through www.sam.gov. Proposals for this Solicitation must be submitted via e-mail in portable document format (PDF). Proposals MUST BE RECEIVED NO LATER THAN stated due date and time in this solicitation. Inquiries concerning this solicitation must be routed to Contracting Officer Natalia Lugo-Vina at natalia.lugo-vinacruz.gsa.gov. Prospective offerors bear sole responsibility for tracking and retrieving the RFP alongside all associated modifications.

The applicable evaluation criteria are also included in the solicitation documents. Project Objective The objective of this acquisition is to restore the existing parking lot to a safe, structurally sound, properly drained, and fully functional condition suitable for use by government employees, visitors, and authorize vehicles. All work shall be completed in accordance with the requirements and specifications identified in the PWS. Location and Time of Performance Southeastern Power Administration, 1166 Athens Tech Drive, Elberton Ga. 30635. The available times are Monday-Friday 6:30am - 5:00pm Site Visit Prospective contractors are strongly encouraged, but not required, to participate in a site visit to assess existing conditions, evaluate the scope of work, and obtain a clear understanding of the project requirements before submitting a quotation. Failure to attend the site visit will not preclude a contractor from submitting a quotation or receiving consideration for award. The vendor has the option to conduct an on-site visit to determine the best approach for Southeastern Power project. Site visits will take place on November 19, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. Eastern Time and November 30, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Please email tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov with your preferred attendance time. Due to security requirements, all attendees must have a valid photo ID (i.e. State Driver's License) with REAL ID compliance to gain access to the site. All contractors must submit a list of attendees at least 24 hours in advance to: tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov. Please ensure that your list includes the name as it appears on your State ID and the company that will be attending. Contractors who do not possess a REAL-ID-compliant form of identification will be denied entry. Contract Type and Award SEPA anticipates awarding one (1) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract for the parking lot repaving and repairing project. The acquisition will be conducted using Simplified Acquisition Procedures in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13, as applicable. Award will be given to the responsible contractor whose proposal represents the best value to the government, based on the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation. Proposal Submission Deadline All proposals must be received by December 15, 2026, no later than 3:00 p.m. (noon), Eastern Standard Time (EST) Proposals may be submitted by mail to: 1166 Athens Tech Rd, Elberton, GA 30635 (addressed to: Tabitha Rambert) or electronically via email to: tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov Questions and Clarifications All questions, answers, requests for clarification, or inquiries concerning this solicitation will be provided to all offerors, posted on sam.gov by December 9, 2026, and shall be directed to both designated Contracting Officers: Primary: Tabitha Rambert, Contracting Officer (tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov) Alternate: Juvonna Mattox, Contracting Officer (juvonna.mattox@sepa.doe.gov) Any changes or clarifications affecting solicitation requirements will be communicated through an official solicitation amendment, as appropriate (via Sam.gov). Submission Timeline Site Visit: November 19, 2026, at 10:30am and November 30, 2026 @1:00 pm, Eastern Time Deadline for submission of all questions will be December 4, 2026 @12:00 pm Eastern time and Deadline for responses will be December 9, 2026, on Sam.gov Bid Submission Deadline: 3pm Eastern Time on December 15, 2026 Expected Decision Date: December 31, 2026 Vendor Start date: Within 30 days of Award Please submit all proposals to the CO via email at: tabitha.rambert@sepa.doe.gov or via mail to:1166 Athens Tech Rd Elberton, GA 30635 before Bid Submission Deadline: 3pm Eastern Time on December 15, 2026. Vendor close-out date: NLT 2 Months from the vendor start date NOTE TO OFFERORS: The Statement of Work (SOW), applicable Wage Determinations, and Aeriel View are incorporated as attachments to this announcement. Offerors are responsible for thoroughly reviewing the solicitation and all accompanying attachments to ensure that their proposals comply with the stated requirements, and all are submitted by the specified deadline. Any amendments to the solicitation will be posted on this website. You are responsible for checking the website periodically. All offerors MUST be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of contract. The Government will evaluate proposals in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and applicable provisions of the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). The Government reserves the right to make an award to the responsible offeror, whose proposal represents the best overall value to the Government, considering the stated evaluation factors.

title: FILTER ELEMENT, FLUID / QPL NSN 1650-00-484-6918 / B-52 AIRCRAFT
description: An Unrestricted solicitation will be issued to establish an Indefinite Quantity Contract (IQC) for NSN 1650-00-484-6918, a FILTER ELEMENT, FLUID. The award will be for a 5-year base period. The Estimated Annual Quantity (EAQ) is 1520 EACH. Production units will be FOB: Destination; Inspection /Acceptance: Origin. Item is critical and deemed an Air Force Critical Safety Item. Surge applies (MWR = 8 each). The proposed contract action is for supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one or a limited number of sources under the authority of FAR 6.302. This is a QPL item IAW BASIC SPEC NR MIL-PRF-83860D NOT 2, REVISION NR D DTD 09/18/2025, PPN: P/N M83860/4-3. Approved QPL sources are PTI Technologies (CAGE 05228) and Pall Aeropower (CAGE 18350). DLA Weapons Support - Richmond does NOT possess complete technical data on this part. There are no other approved sources at this time. Any other interested contractor would have to submit a Source Approval Request (SAR) package for approval to be added as a source by the assigned ESA. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received within forty-five days after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, in its solicitation for the described supplies. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice. This solicitation may include Procurement Note L09, Reverse Auction. Since a reverse auction may be conducted, offerors are encouraged to access the Procurex system and review the reverse auction help tutorials at https//dla.procurexinc.com to learn more about how to participate in an auction. In order to receive an award, regardless of dollar value, contractors must be registered in the System For Award Management (sam.gov). The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The estimated solicitation issue date is 11/13/2026. A copy of the solicitation will be available via DIBBS at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. Choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requesters.

description: Centralizuotos vaizdo stebėjimo sistemos (toliau – VSS) įrangos įsigijimas, jos įrengimas, duomenų perdavimo ir priežiūros paslaugos. Paslaugų teikėjas ne vėliau kaip per 3 (tris) mėnesius nuo Sutarties įsigaliojimo dienos sumontuoja ir sukonfigūruoja pilnai veikiančią VSS, su esamose įrengimo lokacijose nurodytomis vaizdo kameromis (Techninės specifikacijos 1 priedas) ir perduoda naudoti VSS Perkančiajai organizacijai priėmimo-perdavimo aktu. Atsižvelgiant į reikalingą įrengti naują infrastruktūrą, Paslaugų teikėjui suteikiamas ilgesnis 6 (šešių) mėnesių terminas, nuo Sutarties įsigaliojimo dienos, įrengti vaizdo kameras naujose įrengimo lokacijose (Techninės specifikacijos 1 priedas). Per šį laikotarpį turi būti įrengta visa likusi reikalinga įranga su vaizdo kameromis, sukonfigūruota VSS ir pasirašytas šios įrangos dalies priėmimo-perdavimo aktas. VSS duomenų perdavimas, aptarnavimas, techninė priežiūra bei kitų su vaizdo stebėjimo įrangos eksploatacija susijusių paslaugų teikimas vykdomas nuo šios sutarties specialiųjų sąlygų 1 punkte nurodyto priėmimo–perdavimo akto pasirašymo datos iki sutarties galiojimo pabaigos.

title: Germany – Electrical fitting work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - PV-Anlage
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts
